all_quotes.quote: We present a supermassive black hole (SMBH) mass measurement in the Seyfert 1 galaxy NGC 7469 using Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the atomic-${\rm [CI]}$(1-0) and molecular-$^{12}$CO(1-0) emission lines at the spatial resolution of $\approx0.3\ensuremath{''}$ (or $\approx$ 100 pc).

As a follow-up to the ALMA emission-lines survey of the AGN in NGC 7469 (cite: Izumi20), we utilised the bright, high signal-to-noise (S/N) and high-spatial-resolution data of the molecular-$^{12}$CO(1-0) ($\theta_{\rm beam}\approx0.29\ensuremath{''}$) and the atomic-${\rm [CI]}$(1-0) lines ($\theta_{\rm beam}\approx0.31\ensuremath{''}$) to perform cold-gas-dynamical models and weigh the central SMBH.

We present a supermassive black hole (SMBH) mass measurement in the Seyfert 1 galaxy NGC 7469 using Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the atomic-${\rm [CI]}$(1-0) and molecular-$^{12}$CO(1-0) emission lines at the spatial resolution of $\approx0.3\ensuremath{''}$ (or $\approx$ 100 pc).

As is expected from X-ray dominated region (XDR) effects that dramatically increase an atomic carbon abundance by dissociating CO molecules, we suggest that the atomic \[CI\](1-0) emission is a better probe of SMBH masses than CO emission in AGNs.
Given this new $M_{\rm BH}$, we are able to constrain the specific RM dimensionless scaling factor of $f=7.2^{+4.2}_{-3.4}$ for the AGN BLR in NGC 7469.

Regarding this aspect, the $\approx5$% higher in spatial resolution and more extended of $^{12}$CO(1-0) make it a better transition for dynamical modelling than other CO lines. We thus chose the atomic-\[CI\](1-0) and molecular-$^{12}$CO(1-0) emissions among these as the best bets to perform $M_{\rm BH}$ measurement that compromises both these requirements.

Using the dynamics of \[CI\](1-0) and $^{12}$CO(2-1), I20 found $\sigma_{\rm gas}/V_{\rm rot}\approx0.35$ ($r\lesssim0.5\ensuremath{''}$) and $\sigma_{\rm gas}/V_{\rm rot}\approx0.19$ ($r>0.5\ensuremath{''}$) (see panels a and b of their Fig. 11), which indicates a dynamically thin ($d_{\rm t}\approx0$) and cold ($V_{\rm rot}\approx V_{\rm circ}$) CND for NGC 7469.

Accounting for PA variations in our dynamical models help to mimic the warps seen along the galaxy-minor axis of the velocity-field maps of $^{12}$CO(1-0) (panel b of Fig. 2) and \[CI\](1-0) (panel b of Fig. 3).

It is also worth mentioning that the dynamical modeling of the other CO lines observed in this program did not improve the inferred-$M_{\rm BH}$ uncertainty significantly comparing to the chosen $^{12}$CO(1-0).
Additionally, the appearance of the $^{12}$CO(2-1) and $^{12}$CO(3-2) PVDs are similar to that of $^{12}$CO(1-0) PVD. i.e., there would be a “hole” at the AGN position (cite: Smith19; Nguyen20)

Dynamical models with constant PAs will create axisymmetric kinematic maps that cannot well reproduce the data, which are asymmetric along the minor axis. This mismatch between the data and the model biases the $M_{\rm BH}$ estimates and produces some large residuals or artificial non-circular motions in the `Data–Model` maps of the velocity fields.
Here, we rule out the possibility of dust extinction because there is less extinction in this blueshifted component (Section 4.4).

To ensure our fit converges, we ran the model with $3\times10^5$ iterations, then exclude the first 20% of the calculations as the burn-in phase and used the rest 80% to produce the final posterior PDF of all nine free parameters.

Accordingly, in the Bayesian framework, we rescaled the model uncertainties by dividing the model $\log$ likelihood by $\sqrt{2N}$ or equivalently multiplying the `rms` by $(2N)^{1/4}$ (Table \[tab_alma\]).

Given $M_{\rm BH}\approx1.8\times10^7$ M$_{\odot}$ and $\sigma_\star\approx150$ km s$^{-1}$ (cite: Onken04) gives $r_{\rm SOI}\equiv GM_{\rm BH}/\sigma_\star^2\approx3$ pc ($\approx0.01\ensuremath{''}$), a factor of $\approx30$ times smaller than what our ALMA observations can resolve.
Because of the poorly resolvable scale of our data, we argue this consistency applies to the case of NGC 7469 only.
